title: ccd_asi: support at least four ZWO ASI cameras with ST-4 ports
description:
Reported in the CloudMakers forum in November 2026 on INDIGO 3.0-11 with a Raspberry Pi 5: https://bb.cloudmakers.eu/viewtopic.php?p=11240#p11240

The trace shows that the ASI120MM Mini and ASI715MC each attach as a camera and a guider. The server receives the USB arrival event for the ASI183MC, which had attached as both a camera and a guider earlier, but skips it when it is plugged in third. The ccd_asi driver has five logical device slots and requires two free slots to attach a camera with an ST-4 port.

Acceptance criterion: four ST-4-equipped ASI cameras can be attached simultaneously through ccd_asi, and INDIGO enumerates all four cameras and their four corresponding guider devices. Verify the four-camera case with a targeted check.

outcome.summary: Reviewed candidate d18640ba693a67d0c38578a30893488a43d73eaf against master. No concrete defects found. The driver-local max_devices=8 and version increment match generated C; allocation, discovery, removal and shutdown consistently use MAX_DEVICES. The existing fake-SDK regression now verifies four distinct CCD/guider pairs, public INFO interfaces and CONNECTION properties, excess-capacity rejection, slot reuse and cleanup without mocking away production allocation. Documentation accurately states the eight-slot capacity; recorded 54/54 macOS fake-SDK results and before/after reproduction support the change. Additional static inspection confirmed generator attribute handling and clean candidate status. No tests rerun by reviewer; no physical hardware, Linux/Raspberry Pi or Windows runtime validation claimed. The change is minimal and stays within the capacity-only scope.

history.text: Inspecting ASI slot allocation and fake SDK test coverage

Plan: non-interactive fake-SDK/USB validation only; no physical hardware. Extend existing shutdown_pending_discovery_and_capacity case from two ST-4 pairs to four, assert all CCD/guider public INFO and CONNECTION properties and matching masters, retain capacity overflow, slot reuse and shutdown cleanup. Run it against unchanged production source to reproduce failure, then set driver-local max_devices=8, increment version and regenerate. Run the same regression and recorded ccd_asi fake-SDK suite, verify generation stability and configured checks. Scope is capacity only; no SDK, protocol, guider timing or queue redesign.
Building scoped ASI fake-SDK test and reproducing four-camera enumeration failure

Reproduced before production changes on macOS arm64: make Makefile.inc; make init; make -j8 -C indigo_libs all; make -C indigo_test build/integration/test_ccd_asi_sdk succeeded. indigo_test/build/integration/test_ccd_asi_sdk shutdown_pending_discovery_and_capacity failed (exit 1): expected 8, got 4. The existing fake SDK already models eight ST-4 cameras; only the required enumeration expectation changed. Root cause: generated default MAX_DEVICES=5 permits only two camera/guider pairs. No hardware was accessed.
Verifying the eight-slot fix with capacity regression and recorded ASI fake-SDK suite
All 54 ASI cases passed; checking regeneration stability and final configured checks

After fix on macOS arm64: the identical capacity regression passed (exit 0), confirming 4 CCDs plus 4 matching guiders, public INFO interfaces and CONNECTION properties, rejection beyond eight slots, reuse after removal and clean shutdown. Final non-interactive recorded run: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tools/run_driver_test.py ccd_asi passed 54/54 fake-SDK cases and built the production driver; README Testing and TEST_SUMMARY regenerated by the script. Existing integration-case count remains 54, so MIGRATION_STATUS count is unchanged. Repeating indigo_generator produced byte-identical .c/.h/_main.c files. git diff --check passed and make -C indigo_test test-clean removed test binaries. Limitations: no physical cameras, real USB hot-plug, Linux/Raspberry Pi or Windows runtime validation; no throughput or physical ST-4 timing claim. macOS build emitted bundled SDK deployment-target warnings (10.12 objects vs 10.10 target); no ASI test compile errors. Opt-in timing/full repository suites were outside this capacity fix. Hardware tests run: 0.
Reviewing the four-camera capacity change and its fake-SDK regression
